channel.title: EWSR1::FLI1 Suppresses Ribosome Biogenesis and Creates a Targetable Vulnerability in Ewing Sarcoma.
channel.description: Abstract Hyperactive ribosome biogenesis is considered a hallmark of cancer, fueling the rapid growth of tumors. Yet, in Ewing sarcoma (a pediatric bone malignancy driven by the EWSR1::FLI1 fusion oncogene), pathologists have reported non-prominent nucleoli (indicative of attenuated ribosome biogenesis) as a key feature for several decades . Here we investigate this conundrum using a combination of super-resolution microscopy, metabolic labeling of protein synthesis, polysome sequencing, pharmacogenomics, and patient-derived tumor models. We discovered profound nucleolar disorganization marked by clustering of UBF1 and reduction in rRNA levels caused by the fusion oncogene. Mechanistically, EWSR1::FLI1 sequesters endogenous EWSR1, compromising R-loops resolution at the DNA. As a result, R-loops accumulate at rDNA loci, leading to impaired ribosome biogenesis. We further discovered that Ewing sarcoma cells selectively upregulate 5’TOP mRNA translation efficiency to maximize production of the translation machinery in the context of low rRNA availability. Our results establish a unique and fragile mode of protein production in Ewing sarcoma, creating an unexpected and therapeutically promising vulnerability. Indeed, inhibition of translation with etoposide or CX-5461 induce rapid translational collapse and apoptosis in Ewing sarcoma. In summary, our study establishes globally reduced ribosome biogenesis in combination with reduced protein translation as an unexpected oncogenic adaptation in Ewing sarcoma, and it identifies ribosome biogenesis as a pharmacologically targetable Archilles’ heel of this highly fatal bone cancer affecting children and young adults.

item.title: Nucleolus imaging
item.description: We applied confocal and super-resolution STED microscopy to dissect nucleolar organization and ribosome biogenesis in Ewing sarcoma. Confocal imaging enables quantitative assessment of nucleolar size based on UBF1 and NOP58 as nucleolar markers accross large cell populations. STED microscopy provides nanoscale resolution of sub-nucleolar architecture, allowing us to resolve aberrant clustering of UBF1 and structural disorganization of the nucleolus that are not detectable by conventional microscopy. These imaging approaches are central to linking EWSR1::FLI1-driven nucleolar remodeling to impaired ribosome biogenesis and translational vulnerability in Ewing sarcoma.
